extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining, construing, searching, and rejecting or allowing claims that use means- (or step-) plus-function language under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (pre-AIA sixth paragraph). Focuses on definiteness, corresponding structure, written description/enablement, prior-art equivalence, and appropriate prosecution record entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify corresponding structure/material/acts for means-plus-function limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: If one skilled in the art would be able to identify the structure, material or acts from the description in the specification for performing the recited function, then the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (pre-AIA 112, second paragraph) are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 'one skilled in the art' analysis (Atmel; Dossel). Examiner should determine whether the specification disclosure, possibly combined with claims, would permit a POSITA to recognize the structure underlying the recited function (examples: computer + algorithm recognized as a general-purpose computer implementation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require amendment when corresponding structure not identifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: If one skilled in the art would not be able to identify the structure, material or acts from the specification for performing the recited function, applicant must amend the specification to contain the material incorporated by reference, including the clear link or associated structure, material or acts to the function recited in the claim (see 37 CFR 1.57(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should include only the relevant portions of the referenced document corresponding to the means-/step-plus-function limitation to keep the specification concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function indefiniteness often implicates written description and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: A means- (or step-) plus-function limitation found indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) for failure to disclose sufficient corresponding structure may also lack adequate written description and may not be sufficiently enabled to support the full scope of the claim under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre-AIA first paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider whether the disclosure enables a POSITA to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention (see sections MPEP §2161.01, §2164.08). Ariad (genus/function claims) emphasizes demonstrating possession of a functionally-defined genus by describing sufficient species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider entire original disclosure for written description/enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: In assessing 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (written description/enablement) support, examiners must consider the summary, detailed description, original claims, abstract, and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and consider relevant authorities (In re Mott; In re Anderson; Hill-Rom; In re Armbruster; Vas-Cath; In re Wolfensperger) — the full original filing may provide support even if not explicit in one section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere restatement of function in specification is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely restating a function associated with a means-plus-function limitation in the specification, without more description of the means that accomplish the function, is insufficient to provide corresponding structure for definiteness and written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases (Noah; Blackboard; Aristocrat) — specification must describe the means/structure, not just restate the claimed function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims' terms and phrases must have clear support/antecedent basis in description
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1) requires that terms and phrases used in the claims find clear support or antecedent basis in the description so that their meaning may be ascertainable by reference to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the written description implicitly or inherently sets forth corresponding structure, the examiner should either (A) have applicant amend to expressly recite the structure/material/acts, or (B) state on the record what structure/material/acts perform the function — but avoid adding prohibited new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to 'link or associate' structure to function (quid pro quo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure disclosed in the specification is 'corresponding' structure only if the specification or prosecution history clearly links or associates that structure to the function recited in the claim (B. Braun / 35 U.S.C. 112(f) 'quid pro quo').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a POSITA could write software to perform a function, absent a clear link in the specification/prosecution history the software may not be treated as corresponding structure (Medical Instrumentation v. Elekta example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single means claims do not invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and are problematic
rubrics_metrics.description: A single means claim (means-plus-function limitation as the only limitation of a claim) cannot invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) because that provision applies to 'an element in a claim for a combination.' Such single-means claims are not limited to the structure/material/acts disclosed in the specification and thus may cover every conceivable means to perform the function, making them potentially nonenabling under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Hyatt — single-means claims that read on subject matter not enabled by the specification should be rejected under 112(a). Distinguish multiple functional limitations (each is a separate element).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret multiple functional limitations as separate 112(f) elements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim uses a generic placeholder (e.g., 'system') to recite a series of functions, each function should be interpreted as a separate section 112(f) limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 'system configured to extract' and 'system configured to compare' — treat as two separate elements invoking 112(f) where 'system' serves as a non-structural placeholder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must state when 35 U.S.C. 112(f) is being applied and identify corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner interprets a claim limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the Office action should specify that determination and indicate what the specification identifies as the corresponding structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corresponding structure is not clearly identifiable, the Office action should still attempt to identify the structure most closely associated with the means-/step-plus-function limitation to facilitate a prior art search. If applicant disagrees, they may present showing or amend claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions and 3-prong analysis for invoking 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation that explicitly uses 'means' with functional language triggers a presumption that 35 U.S.C. 112(f) applies; conversely, lack of the term 'means' triggers a presumption it does not. These presumptions are rebuttable and examiners should apply them along with the 3-prong analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the record for the presumption and 3-prong analysis; state the interpretation in the Office action so applicant/public are notified and can respond or amend to avoid 112(f) interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: On allowance, indicate 112(f) interpretation and associated structure
rubrics_metrics.description: When allowing a claim that was treated under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the examiner should indicate in the reasons for allowance that the claim was interpreted under 112(f) and clarify the associated structure if not previously made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps public notice and clarifies claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art application to means-plus-function requires identical function and sound basis for equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying prior art to a means-/step-plus-function limitation requires that the prior art element perform the identical function specified in the claim; if the prior art only teaches identity of function, the examiner bears the initial burden to show the prior art structure or step is the same as or equivalent to the corresponding structure/material/acts described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art teaches the identical structure but is silent about performing the claimed function, a reasonable presumption of inherent performance may be appropriate, but examiner must provide a 'sound basis for believing' the prior art structure would be capable of performing the claimed function (see MPEP §2114 and In re Spada).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors supporting a conclusion that a prior art element is an equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors include: (A) prior art performs the identical function in substantially the same way and produces substantially the same results; (B) a POSITA would recognize interchangeability of the prior art element for the corresponding disclosed element; (C) insubstantial differences between the prior art element and the corresponding disclosed element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases (Kemco; Odetics; Lockheed; Deere; Al-Site; Chiuminatta; IMS; Warner-Jenkinson). Examiner should explain the rationale when concluding equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: If examiner shows equivalence, explain rationale and then applicant bears burden to prove nonequivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner finds the prior art element equivalent, the Office action should explain why; once a prima facie case of equivalence is made, the burden shifts to applicant to show the prior art element is not an equivalent of the structure/material/acts described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may respond with teachings in specification, teachings in prior art, or 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit evidence; examiner should then weigh the indicia and evidence presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Even if nonequivalence is shown, examiner must consider obviousness (35 U.S.C. 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding of nonequivalence preventing anticipation does not preclude a determination that the claimed means-/step-plus-function limitation is obvious from the prior art; the examiner must still perform a 103 analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative grounds of rejection may be appropriate; examiner may apply 102/103 where appropriate despite equivalence issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification silence on equivalents can shift burden to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification is silent as to what constitutes equivalents and the examiner has made a prima facie case of equivalence, the burden is on the applicant to show that a prior art element which performs the claimed function is not an equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Mulder and In re Noll; applicant's explanations should be consistent with the specification disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere allegations of nonequivalence are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Bare statements or opinions that a prior art element is not an equivalent are not persuasive; the examiner should consider and weigh presented indicia and determine whether applicant has met the burden of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should provide substantive evidence (specification teachings, prior art teachings, affidavits under 37 CFR 1.132). If applicant's proposed limiting interpretation is inconsistent with the specification, examiner should require amendment to recite specific structural/functional characteristics before allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'equivalents' depends on how element is described in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An equivalent embraces more than the specific elements described in the specification for performing the function but less than any element that performs the function; scope varies depending on whether specification limits to particular embodiments or describes broader equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one embodiment is described, corresponding structure may be limited to that embodiment and equivalents thereof (NOMOS). If the disclosure is so broad as to encompass any and all structures, then 'equivalents' cease to limit claim scope and claims must be read accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants may amend claims to avoid 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to an Office action invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f), applicant may (1) present a sufficient showing to establish that the claim limitation recites sufficient structure to avoid interpretation under 112(f), or (2) amend the claim to recite sufficient structure (or otherwise avoid the limitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments might include reciting specific structure/material/acts or narrowing the functional language; see MPEP §2187 for form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: When making a prior art search for means-plus-function limitations, attempt to identify corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate a prior art search, Office actions should identify the corresponding structure for the claimed function; if not clearly identifiable, the examiner should attempt to identify the most closely associated structure in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps locate prior art and clarifies for applicant what is being compared; if multiple disclosed implementations exist, clarify which supports the limitation (see subsection II.B).
